paragraphs.text: A DeepSeek Harness web plugin that adds a Model Hub settings page for configuring
# dsh-plugin-model-hub

A DeepSeek Harness web plugin that adds a
**Model Hub** settings page for configuring:

- every provider's profile fields (`displayName`, `api`, `baseURL`, `models`) in
`settings.yaml`,
-

per-provider and per-model **context windows** (`defaultContextWindow` on the
provider, `contextWind

ow` on each model — the value the web UI shows as the
context budget, so a 1M-token model displays 1

M instead of the 256K pi-ai
default),
- per-provider **API keys** (stored through the credentials se

rvice, never
written into `settings.yaml`),
- per-provider **API-error retry/backoff tuning** (max r

etries, initial/max
wait, jitter, retryable error codes) — the knobs
`dsh-llm-retry` executes,
- the

**default Agent model**, and
- declaring brand-new pi-ai provider routes (an OpenAI-compatible gate

way or any
protocol `dsh-llm-pi-ai` supports).
## Why this page exists

The built-in Models settings page reads and writes through the loopback-only
**settings mirror**, wh

ich is deliberately unavailable when the GUI is served
over insecure HTTPS or a non-loopback origin

("settings are unavailable in this
browser"). This plugin does **not** depend on that mirror: every

read and write
goes straight over the wire through the stock `settings`, `credentials`, and
`llm` RP
C domains, so the page works on any origin the harness itself can reach.
## How it works
The package is a **dual-face cordis plugin**:

- **host half** (`lib/index.js`) — a stub entry that exists so the package is a
real loader entry in

the profile. The web app's client-modules scan only
discovers client bundles for packages that are

active loader entries declaring
`dsh.client`.
- **client half** (`lib/client.js`) — the browser page

and its data layer,
registered into the `settings.section` slot. It talks to the harness through
th
e stock RPC domains; no custom transport is needed.
## Install

The plugin ships with a bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml`) that inserts one
loader row, `model-config
`. Two equivalent install paths:
### 1. Via `dsh plugin` (recommended)
From a checkout at `<checkout>`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`dsh plugin` runs `pnpm add` in the profile directory, then reconciles the
profile's `dsh.profile.bu

ndles` layer list: any dependency whose manifest
declares `dsh.bundle` (this one does) joins the bun
dle layers automatically.

For local development, prefer a symlinked spec so source edits take effect
without reinstalling:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### 2. Manually

- Add `dsh-plugin-model-hub` to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` in
`~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.

json` **and** make it resolvable from the profile
(e.g. `pnpm --dir ~/.dsh/profiles/web add file:/pa

th/to/dsh-plugin-model-hub`),
**or**
- merge the row from `cordis.patch.yml` into the profile's
`~/.
dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` yourself.

Then restart the profile (`dsh web`) — the client-modules scan runs at
activation, so a fresh boot i
s required to pick up a new bundle.
## Using the page

The **Model Config** section appears in Settings (next to the built-in
sections). For each provider

Config** section appears in Settings (next to the built-in
sections). For each provider row you can:

- see whether a credential is configured,
- edit profile fields and models,
- enter or replace the A

PI key (leaving it blank keeps the stored one),
- override the retry policy — unset fields keep `dsh

-llm` defaults
(normal mode, 5 retries, 500 ms → 10 s exponential backoff, 10% jitter),
- delete a p
rovider whose profile is user-defined (and its stored key).
## Development

store, write paths, and
retry-policy building are covered without a browser.
